title: 1976 AHSME Problem 22
statement: Given an equilateral triangle with side of length \(s,\) consider the locus of all points \(P\) in the plane of the triangle such that the sum of the squares of the distances from \(P\) to the vertices of the triangle is a fixed number \(a.\) This locus

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
contains only three points if \(a=2s^2\) and is a circle if
\(a\gt2s^2\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
is a circle with positive radius only if \(s^2\lt
a\lt2s^2\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
contains only a finite number of points for any value of
\(a\)

solutions.text:
For vertices \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) with centroid \(G,\) put \(T=GA^2+GB^2+GC^2.\) The standard centroid identity gives \[ PA^2+PB^2+PC^2=3PG^2+T. \] In an equilateral triangle, each \(GA=\frac{s}{\sqrt3},\) so \(T=s^2.\) Hence \(3PG^2=a-s^2.\) The locus is empty for \(a\lt s^2,\) one point for \(a=s^2,\) and a circle of positive radius for \(a\gt s^2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(G\) be the centroid and express the sum using \(PG^2\)
For an equilateral triangle, the sum equals \(3PG^2+s^2\)
